reception: What traveled is the argument rather than any artifact. The small citing literature invokes the keynote almost entirely as evidence: the pipeline-parallelism line of Giacomoni, Vachharajani, and colleagues, from FastForward through its companion reports, cites it for the premise that multicores shift the burden of performance onto software, and work on visualizing potential parallelism and on teaching multicore programming uses it the same way. Every judged citation is peripheral, and none builds on the talk itself — the expected shape for a keynote abstract whose diagnosis was becoming common ground.
